editorial:
Imagine living a life where you feel stuck, and the only way to be happy is to be someone else in a completely different country. That is exactly what happens here. You meet Ruben, who is living in Cuba, and Andy, who left Cuba years ago to live in the United States. Even though they are thousands of miles apart, they both feel like they are in a cage. Ruben wants the freedom and wealth of the US, while Andy misses his home and feels lonely in a place that doesn't truly accept him. It is a sad but interesting look at how politics and history can rip people's lives apart, making them crave a life they can never actually have.

The acting is really grounded and makes you feel the frustration of both men. The pacing is a bit slow since it focuses more on feelings than big action scenes, but that is why it works. You will probably find yourself wondering what you would do in their shoes. If you can find a high-quality digital copy to rent on Apple TV, it is definitely worth the watch. If you are a movie collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move to keep this hidden gem safe. It is perfect for anyone who likes stories about family and longing.
endingExplained: In the end, you see that neither man can truly escape their situation. They spend the whole movie dreaming of switching places, but the political walls between Cuba and the US are too high. The final scenes show them still trapped in their own worlds, realizing that the grass is not always greener on the other side. They remain separated by history, leaving you with a bittersweet feeling that some gaps can never be closed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves human stories and historical dramas.
